parole.significato: wild pear (Pyrus elaeagrifolia or Pyrus pyraster – the tree or its fruit)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آخلاط (ahlat), from Byzantine Greek ἀχλάδιον (akhládion). Compare Greek αχλάδι (achládi).
From Ottoman Turkish آلای (alay), from Byzantine Greek ἀλλάγιον (allágion).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پودروم (bodrum, podrum), borrowed from Byzantine Greek ὑπόδρομος (hupódromos, literally “under-walkway”).

From Ottoman Turkish بره (bre), from Byzantine Greek βρέ (bré) (compare modern Greek βρε (vre) and ρε (re), Serbo-Croatian bre, Albanian bre), probably shortened from μωρέ (mōré, “man!”, literally “fool!”) (modern Greek μωρέ (moré)), a frozen vocative of Ancient Greek μωρός (mōrós, “stupid”).

parole.significato: fishgarth, fishweir, or a fishing station on poles above the water where one looks out for fish and leads them into nets
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طالیان (dalyan, “fishweir, fishgarth”), presumed to derive from Byzantine Greek *ἁλιάνειον (*haliáneion, “fishing place”).

parole.significato: rudder (used to steer a vessel or aircraft)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish دومن (dümen), from Byzantine Greek τιμόνι (timóni).
From Ottoman Turkish فدان (fidan), from Byzantine Greek φυτόν (phutón, “plant”).

parole.significato: brush, any implement made of bristles used for cleaning
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فرچه (fırča), from Byzantine Greek βρούτζα (broútza).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فوچی (fuçi, fıçı), borrowed from Byzantine Greek βούττις (boúttis, “barrel, cask”), from Ancient Greek βοῦττῐς (boûttĭs), possibly borrowed from Pre-Greek.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوندر (gönder, günder, “pole, shaft”), from Byzantine Greek κοντάριν (kontárin, “pole, spar”), from Ancient Greek κοντάριον (kontárion), diminutive of κοντός (kontós, “spear”). Cognate to Greek κοντάρι (kontári, “pole, spar; flagpole”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كمرك (gümrük), borrowed from Byzantine Greek κομμέρκιον (kommérkion), borrowed from Latin commercium, from con- (“together, with”) + merx (“merchandise”) + -ium.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خلاط (halat, “hawser, rope”), itself from Byzantine Greek καλόδιο (kalódio, “rope”).

parole.significato: a type of folk dance in Turkey
parole.testo: From alay (“crowd”), from Ottoman Turkish آلای (alay, “crowd”), from Byzantine Greek ἀλάγιον (alágion).
From Ottoman Turkish قادرغه, from Byzantine Greek κάτεργον (kátergon, “galley; penal labor”), from Ancient Greek κάτεργος (kátergos).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كدی (kedi), from Byzantine Greek γατί (gatí, “kitten”), ultimately from Latin cattus. Related to English cat. Replaced native pisi, which is now often child-speak, archaism, or vocative interjection.
From Ottoman Turkish كركنس (kerkenes), from Byzantine Greek κερχνηίς (kerkhnēís), variant of κέρχνη (kérkhnē).

parole.significato: chestnut, the edible nut-like fruit of the tree Castanea sativa
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كستانه (kestane), from Byzantine Greek κᾰ́στᾰνᾰ (kắstănă), ultimately from Ancient Greek κᾰ́στᾰνᾰ (kắstănă, “sweet chestnuts”).

parole.significato: pantry, larder, storeroom, cellar, a small room, closet, or cabinet where food and beverages are stored
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلار (kilar, kiler, “pantry”), from Byzantine Greek κελλάριν (kellárin), from Koine Greek κελλάριον (kellárion), ultimately from Latin cellārium (“storeroom, larder, pantry”).
From Ottoman Turkish كلیسا (kilisa), from Byzantine Greek ἐκκλησίᾱ (ekklēsíā).

parole.significato: rooftile, a tile put on a roof to keep out rain or snow
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرمید (kiremid, “rooftile”), itself from Byzantine Greek κεραμίδι (keramídi), from Ancient Greek κερᾰμῐ́δῐον (kerămĭ́dĭon, “small tile”). Doublet of seramik.
From Ottoman Turkish قونسلوس (konsolos), from Byzantine Greek κόνσουλος (kónsoulos), from Latin cōnsul.
From Ottoman Turkish كوكنار, from Byzantine Greek κουκουναριά (koukounariá).

parole.significato: cabbage, an edible plant of the species Brassica oleracea having a head of green leaves
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لحنه (lahana, “cabbage”), from Byzantine Greek λάχανα (lákhana), plural of λάχανον (lákhanon, “garden herb, vegetable”).
From Ottoman Turkish لیمان (liman), from Byzantine Greek λιμένιον (liménion), from Ancient Greek λιμήν (limḗn).

parole.significato: puerpera, a woman who has just given birth or who is recovering from childbirth
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لخوسه (lohusa), from Byzantine Greek λεχώνα (lekhṓna), from Ancient Greek λεχώ (lekhṓ). Compare Greek λεχώνα (lechóna).
From Ottoman Turkish مارت, from Byzantine Greek Μᾱ́ρτιος (Mā́rtios), from Latin martius.

parole.significato: lettuce, any edible plant in the genus Lactuca and its leaves, eaten as a vegetable
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مارول (marul), from Byzantine Greek μαρούλιον (maroúlion).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مغازه (mağâza), borrowed from Byzantine Greek μαγαζίον (magazíon), borrowed from Venetan magazén, borrowed from Arabic مَخَازِن (maḵāzin), from مَخْزَن (maḵzan), from خَزَنَ (ḵazana). Doublet of mahzen, magazin, and mağazi.
From Ottoman Turkish ناملو (namlu), from older ناملی (namlı), by metathesis from Byzantine Greek [Term?] (modern Greek λαμνί (lamní)), from Latin lamina.

parole.significato: hawser, mooring rope used in docking a ship
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پالامار (palamar, “hawser”), from Byzantine Greek παλαμάριον (palamárion). See Greek παλαμάρι (palamári).

parole.significato: Atlantic bonito, any large, mackerel-like fish of the species Sarda sarda
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پالاموت (palamut, “Atlantic bonito”), from Byzantine Greek παλαμίδα (palamída, “Atlantic bonito”), from Ancient Greek πηλαμύς (pēlamús, “young tunny”).

From Ottoman Turkish پاپادیا (“wife of a priest; camomile”), from a Byzantine Greek ancestor of modern Greek παπαδιά (papadiá, “wife of a priest”). For the sense development compare Middle Armenian իրիցուկ (iricʻuk).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پلیچ (piliç, “pullet”), from Byzantine Greek [Term?] (modern Greek πουλίτσα (poulítsa)), from Ancient Greek πῶλος (pôlos).
From Ottoman Turkish صافره, from Byzantine Greek σαβούρα (saboúra).
From Ottoman Turkish سالیا (salya), from older سالیار (salyar), from Byzantine Greek σάλιον (sálion) (modern Greek σαλιά (saliá)).
From Ottoman Turkish صندال (sandal), from Byzantine Greek σανδάλιον (sandálion).

parole.significato: sea sponge, any of various marine invertebrates of the phylum Porifera
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سونكر (sünger, “sponge”), from Byzantine Greek σφουγγάριον (sphoungárion), from Ancient Greek σπόγγος (spóngos), ultimately from a Pre-Greek substrate.

parole.significato: A fine silver thread, with or without gilding.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صیرمه (ṣırma, “silver or silvergilt thread or lace”), from Byzantine Greek σύρμα (súrma, “gold or silver thread”), Ancient Greek σύρω (súrō, “to draw, to trail”). Cognates with Azerbaijani sırma.
From Ottoman Turkish اخلامور (ıhlamur), فلامور (fılamur), ultimately from Byzantine Greek. See the Ottoman entry for more.

parole.significato: a male farmhand, a male agricultural labourer, a male servant
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ارغات (ırgat), from Byzantine Greek εργάτης (ergátēs), from Ancient Greek ἐργάτης (ergátēs).
From Ottoman Turkish اِسْتٰاقۆسْ (ıstakos), from Byzantine Greek ἀστακός m (astakós). Compare Greek αστακός (astakós).
